editorial.title: 학대 피해 아동이 경찰에 신고했는데도 숨지다니
editorial.body: (사설) 천안 아동학대 사망 사건은 반복된 학대 신고와 명확한 증거에도 불구하고 경찰, 지자체, 법원 등 관계 당국의 미흡한 대응으로 비극이 발생한 사례다. 아동학대 예방, 아동보호, 기관의 적극적 개입, 사회적 책임 등이 강조된다. |

아동보호 시스템 강화와 사회적 책임 촉구한다.
editorial.pullQuote: 반복된 학대 신고와 명확한 증거에도 불구하고 관계 당국의 미흡한 대응으로 비극이 발생했다.
editorial.stance: 아동학대 신고 후에도 사망하는 사건을 막기 위해 관계 기관의 적극적 개입과 실효성 있는 보호 체계 구축이 시급하다.
editorial.titleTr: Child abuse victim dies despite reporting to police
summaryTr: A child abuse case in Cheonan ended in tragedy even after police were notified.
Police, local authorities, and courts all fell short in their response.
There is an urgent call to strengthen the child protection system and ensure social responsibility.
editorial.bodyTr: The child abuse death case in Cheonan is a tragic example where multiple institutions—including police, local government, and courts—failed to respond adequately despite repeated reports of abuse and clear evidence. The incident underscores the critical importance of child abuse prevention, child protection, active institutional intervention, and social responsibility.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Government's Real Estate Battle Already Lost, Yet Stubbornly Insists "Policy Beats Market
summaryTr: Land minister sparks controversy by claiming government policy can control the market.
Real estate policy failures highlight fixation on idea that 'policy beats the market.'
Suggests inducing private supply and Tokyo model instead of punitive taxation.
editorial.bodyTr: Land Minister Kim Yun-deok's remarks suggesting that government policy can control the market have raised concerns about the failure of real estate policy. editorials.titleTr: Editorial: China's Spy Threat Now Targets Fighter Jets, Outpacing Hostile Nations
summaryTr: Former Chinese People's Liberation Army operatives attempted to eavesdrop on U.S. military intelligence at military bases in Pyeongtaek and Gunsan.
Chinese espionage activities are expanding across multiple fronts, including drone surveillance and recruitment of operatives.
Concerns mount over gaps in domestic counterintelligence systems and weakened security response capabilities following the transfer of investigative authority.
editorials.bodyTr: Chinese nationals with ties to the People's Liberation Army have been arrested for attempting to gather intelligence on U.S. military forces and conduct wiretapping operations at key military bases including Pyeongtaek and Gunsan. As China's espionage activities expand across multiple fronts through drone surveillance and asset recruitment, concerns are mounting over gaps in the nation's counterintelligence system and diminished security response capabilities following the transfer of investigative authority.

[뉴스1] 경기도가 재정 비상 선언(5일)을 하며 이미 정해진 예산마저 깎는 ‘감액 추경’에 나섰다. 인구 1420만 명의 전국 최대 광역 지자체 재정 상황이 “마른 땅에 풀 한 포기조차 남지 않았다”(추미애 지사)고 비유할 정도라니 충격적이긴 하지만 실은 예고된 사태이기도 하다. 재정 상황이 나빠진 배경에 대해 추 지사는 “중앙정부가 경기도에 교부세를 주지 않아 재정 둑이 무너져도 메울 수가 없다”고 불만을 토로했다. 추 지사는 반도체 기업들이 납부하는 법인지방소득세(연 1조~3조원)를 용인·화성·평택·이천·수원 등 기초 지자체가 모두 가져간다면서 세수의 합리적 배분도 촉구했다. 추 지사의 주장이 타당한지 여부는 더 따져봐야 할 문제지만, 재정 악화의 근본적 원인은 수입보다 지출에서 찾는 게 맞는 순서다. 가정이든 지자체든 국가든 수입에 맞춰 지출 계획을 짜고 실행하는 것이야말로 살림살이의 기본이고, 이를 어기면 어김없이 위기가 온다. 경기도는 2014년 취임한 남경필 지사 재임 기간 부채를 2조원 이상 감축했다. 그러다 이재명 지사 재임 기간에 재난기본소득 집행, 지역화폐 발행 등의 영향으로 부채 규모가 1조원 이상 증가했다. 청년기본소득과 지역화폐 발행 정책을 이어받은 김동연 지사 재임 4년 동안 복지예산은 14조원에서 19조6000억원으로 급증했다. 이를 감당하기 위해 경기도는 지방채를 대거 발행하고 각종 기금을 일반회계로 돌려 쓰다가 위기로 내몰렸다. 재정 악화의 여파로 노인·아동·임산부 등 민생 예산에 차질을 빚을 상황이다. 올해 본예산이 처음 40조원을 돌파한 경기도의 예산 대비 채무비율은 15.5%여서 아직 행정안전부가 정한 재정 위기 수준은 아니다. 하지만 재정자립도가 44%로 전국 평균(32.3%)을 웃도는 경기도가 재정 비상을 선언했으니 다른 지자체는 채무 부담이 더 클 수 있다. 예컨대 대전광역시는 지난 4년간 지방채 5800억원이 증가하자 재정 혁신 계획을 내놨다. 경기도가 울린 비상벨이 거기서 그쳐선 안 된다. 방만한 재정 운용과 선심성 퍼주기 경쟁이 어떤 사태를 초래하는지 경기도를 반면교사로 삼아야 할 것이다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Gyeonggi Province Declares Financial Emergency...Reckless Spending, Not Tax Revenue, Is the Real Problem
summaryTr: Gyeonggi Province has declared a financial emergency and begun cutting its budget.
The main cause is a sharp increase in welfare spending from 14 trillion won to 19.6 trillion won.
The province must adhere to basic fiscal principles of reducing expenditures to match revenues.
editorial.bodyTr:
Gyeonggi Province declared a fiscal emergency last Tuesday and has begun cutting already-approved budgets through supplementary budget reductions. The financial situation of the nation's largest metropolitan local government, with a population of 14.2 million, has become so dire that Governor Choo Mi-ae likened it to "not a single blade of grass left on parched earth." While shocking, this was ultimately a foreseeable crisis.

Governor Choo attributed the deteriorating finances to the central government, saying "the central government does not allocate transfer taxes to Gyeonggi Province, so we cannot fill the breach even if the fiscal levee collapses." She also called for a more rational distribution of tax revenue, pointing out that basic local governments in Yongin, Hwaseong, Pyeongtaek, Icheon, and Suwon collect all of the corporate local income taxes paid by semiconductor companies, which amounts to 1 to 3 trillion won annually.

Whether Governor Choo's claims are justified requires further examination, but the root cause of fiscal deterioration should be traced to expenditures exceeding revenues. For any household, local government, or nation, budgeting expenditures in line with income is the fundamental principle of sound finances. Violating this principle inevitably invites crisis.

During Governor Nam Kyung-pul's tenure beginning in 2014, Gyeonggi Province reduced debt by over 2 trillion won. However, during Governor Lee Jae-myung's administration, debt increased by over 1 trillion won due to emergency basic income programs and regional currency issuance. During Governor Kim Dong-yeon's four-year tenure, which continued these youth basic income and regional currency policies, welfare spending surged from 14 trillion won to 19.6 trillion won. To manage this, Gyeonggi Province issued local bonds on a massive scale and diverted various funds from special accounts to the general account, ultimately pushing itself into crisis.

As the fiscal situation deteriorates, essential public spending on the elderly, children, and pregnant women faces disruptions. Though Gyeonggi Province's debt-to-budget ratio of 15.5% has not yet reached the fiscal crisis level set by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, and its fiscal self-reliance rate of 44 percent exceeds the national average of 32.3 percent, the province's declaration of fiscal emergency suggests that other local governments face even heavier debt burdens. Daejeon Metropolitan City, for instance, announced a fiscal innovation plan after its local bonds increased by 580 billion won over the past four years.

Gyeonggi Province's alarm bell must not stop ringing there. The reckless fiscal management and competitive largesse spending demonstrated by Gyeonggi Province should serve as a cautionary tale for all local governments.

editorial.title: Underfunded mandates
editorial.body: Government must honor statutory funding before raising health insurance premiums A health insurance system can survive an aging population. What it cannot survive indefinitely is a government that treats its own funding obligation as optional. South Korea’s national health insurance system is offering an early warning. In the first quarter, the system recorded a current account deficit of 3.9 trillion won ($2.8 billion), ending five consecutive years of annual surpluses. Its accumulated reserves fell from 30.22 trillion won at the end of 2025 to 26.32 trillion won three months later. The government had expected the system to move into deficit this year. The speed of the deterioration is troubling. So are the demographic pressures driving costs higher. People aged 65 and older accounted for 44.1 percent of medical spending in 2023. That share is projected to rise to 53.1 percent by 2030 and 70.2 percent by 2050. Meanwhile, the population paying premiums through employment is shrinking. Medical demand is rising as the pool financing it contracts. The obvious response is to raise premiums. Yet that answer becomes less convincing when the state itself has failed to meet its legal share. Under the National Health Insurance Act and the National Health Promotion Act, the government is required to provide an amount equivalent to 20 percent of estimated annual premium revenue, with 14 percent coming from the general account and 6 percent from the National Health Promotion Fund. From 2007 through 2024, however, the government never met that statutory level. Its actual contribution stayed around 13 to 14 percent, leaving an estimated 22 trillion won gap. Over the past five years, the government reportedly underestimated health insurance premium revenue by 9.8 trillion won. Since the statutory contribution is linked to estimated revenue, understating the base conveniently reduces the state’s obligation. The Lee Jae Myung administration has acknowledged the problem. Yet its first budget allocated support equivalent to 14.2 percent of expected premium revenue, down from 14.4 percent the previous year. Asking households to pay more while the state pays less than the law requires is difficult to defend. Nor should health insurance reserves become a convenient second budget for government policy. More than 8.6 trillion won has been drawn from the insurance fund for measures including emergency medical support and hospital restructuring. Such transfers may be defensible in an emergency, but repeated reliance on them blurs the line between social insurance and general taxation. More government funding alone will not make premium increases unnecessary. Korea’s per capita health spending, at $5,099 on a purchasing-power-parity basis, remains below the OECD average of $6,097. An aging society will require more resources. Higher premiums may therefore be unavoidable. But additional revenue should come with a more disciplined healthcare system. Korea needs stronger primary care and better management of chronic disease, while expensive tertiary hospitals should concentrate on serious and complex cases. Wasteful testing, duplicate treatment and improper claims also deserve closer scrutiny. A fee-for-service system makes cost control harder as an aging population requires more frequent treatment and more complex care. Alternative revenues, such as the Center for Market Education’s proposal to raise cigarette prices, could provide some breathing room. Useful as that may be, it is a buffer, not a long-term financing model. The government should first make its 20 percent obligation enforceable against settled revenue figures rather than flexible estimates. It should also require legislative approval for major transfers from National Health Insurance Service reserves to broader government programs. Korea’s health insurance problem is both demographic and institutional. Before asking citizens to pay higher premiums, the government should stop putting less into the system than the law requires. A sustainable safety net begins with an honest ledger, rather than price increases that merely paper over the underlying fiscal strain. 보험료 인상 부담을 지면서도 정부가 법적 의무를 외면한다면 정당성을 찾기 어렵다. 고령화 사회는 보건의료 시스템이 감당할 수 있다. 그러나 자신의 재정 의무를 선택사항처럼 다루는 정부는 그 시스템을 무한정 유지할 수 없다. 한국의 국민건강보험제도가 조기 경고를 발령하고 있다. 1분기에 건강보험은 3조9000억원의 당기적자를 기록했으며, 5년 연속 연간 흑자는 끝났다. 누적 적립금은 2025년 말 30조2200억원에서 3개월 뒤 26조3200억원으로 떨어졌다. 정부는 올해 적자로 돌아설 것으로 예상했다. 악화 속도가 우려스럽다. 비용을 높이는 인구통계학적 압박도 마찬가지다. 65세 이상 인구가 2023년 의료비 지출의 44.1퍼센트를 차지했다. 이 비율은 2030년 53.1퍼센트, 2050년 70.2퍼센트로 증가할 것으로 예상된다. 한편 고용을 통해 보험료를 내는 인구는 줄어들고 있다. 의료 수요는 증가하는데 이를 재정하는 집단은 축소되고 있다. 당연한 대응은 보험료를 인상하는 것이다. 그러나 국가 자체가 법정 의무를 이행하지 못했을 때 그 대답의 설득력은 약해진다.

국민건강보험법과 국민건강증진법에 따르면 정부는 예상 연간 보험료 수입의 20퍼센트에 해당하는 금액을 제공해야 하며, 일반회계에서 14퍼센트, 국민건강증진기금에서 6퍼센트를 내야 한다. 그러나 2007년부터 2024년까지 정부는 법정 수준을 한 번도 충족하지 못했다. 실제 기여는 13~14퍼센트 수준에 머물렀으며, 추정 격차는 22조원이다. 지난 5년간 정부는 건강보험료 수입을 9조8000억원 과소 추정한 것으로 알려졌다. 법정 기여가 추정 수입과 연동되므로 기초를 낮게 잡으면 정부의 의무를 편리하게 줄일 수 있다. 이재명 행정부는 이 문제를 인정했다. 그러나 첫 예산안은 예상 보험료 수입의 14.2퍼센트에 해당하는 지원을 배정했으며, 이는 전년도 14.4퍼센트보다 낮다.

건강보험 적립금이 정부 정책의 편리한 두 번째 예산이 되어서도 안 된다. 응급의료 지원과 병원 구조조정을 포함한 여러 조치를 위해 보험기금에서 8조6000억원 이상이 인출되었다. 이러한 이전은 긴급 상황에서는 정당화될 수 있지만, 반복적인 의존은 사회보험과 일반세제 사이의 경계를 모호하게 한다. 정부 자금 증가만으로는 보험료 인상을 불필요하게 만들지 못한다. 한국의 1인당 보건의료 지출은 구매력 평가 기준 5099달러로 OECD 평균 6097달러보다 여전히 낮다. 고령 사회는 더 많은 자원을 필요로 할 것이다. 따라서 보험료 인상은 불가피할 수 있다. 그러나 추가 수입은 더욱 규율 있는 의료 시스템과 함께 와야 한다. 한국은 강화된 1차 진료와 만성질환 관리가 필요하며, 비용이 많이 드는 3차 병원은 심각하고 복잡한 증례에 집중해야 한다. 낭비적 검사, 중복 치료, 부당 청구도 더 면밀히 검토할 가치가 있다. 행위별 수가제는 고령 인구가 더 자주 치료받고 더 복잡한 치료가 필요해지면서 비용 통제를 더 어렵게 한다. 담배 가격 인상을 제안하는 시장교육센터의 제안 같은 대체 수입원은 숨을 고를 여유를 제공할 수 있다. 그것이 유용할 수 있지만, 이는 일시적 버팀목이지 장기 재정 모델이 아니다. 정부는 먼저 유연한 추정치가 아니라 확정된 수입에 대해 20퍼센트 의무를 강제할 수 있도록 해야 한다. 또한 국민건강보험공단 적립금을 더 광범위한 정부 프로그램으로 이전할 때 입법 승인을 요구해야 한다. 한국의 건강보험 문제는 인구통계학적이자 제도적이다. 국민에게 더 높은 보험료를 내라고 하기 전에 정부는 법이 요구하는 것보다 덜 시스템에 투입하는 것을 멈춰야 한다. 지속 가능한 안전망은 기저의 재정 압박을 가리기만 하는 가격 인상이 아니라 정직한 회계에서 비롯된다.

editorials.title: Underfunded mandates
editorials.body: Government must honor statutory funding before raising health insurance premiums A health insurance system can survive an aging population. What it cannot survive indefinitely is a government that treats its own funding obligation as optional. South Korea’s national health insurance system is offering an early warning. In the first quarter, the system recorded a current account deficit of 3.9 trillion won ($2.8 billion), ending five consecutive years of annual surpluses. Its accumulated reserves fell from 30.22 trillion won at the end of 2025 to 26.32 trillion won three months later. The government had expected the system to move into deficit this year. The speed of the deterioration is troubling. So are the demographic pressures driving costs higher. People aged 65 and older accounted for 44.1 percent of medical spending in 2023. That share is projected to rise to 53.1 percent by 2030 and 70.2 percent by 2050. Meanwhile, the population paying premiums through employment is shrinking. Medical demand is rising as the pool financing it contracts. The obvious response is to raise premiums. Yet that answer becomes less convincing when the state itself has failed to meet its legal share. Under the National Health Insurance Act and the National Health Promotion Act, the government is required to provide an amount equivalent to 20 percent of estimated annual premium revenue, with 14 percent coming from the general account and 6 percent from the National Health Promotion Fund. From 2007 through 2024, however, the government never met that statutory level. Its actual contribution stayed around 13 to 14 percent, leaving an estimated 22 trillion won gap. Over the past five years, the government reportedly underestimated health insurance premium revenue by 9.8 trillion won. Since the statutory contribution is linked to estimated revenue, understating the base conveniently reduces the state’s obligation. The Lee Jae Myung administration has acknowledged the problem. Yet its first budget allocated support equivalent to 14.2 percent of expected premium revenue, down from 14.4 percent the previous year. Asking households to pay more while the state pays less than the law requires is difficult to defend. Nor should health insurance reserves become a convenient second budget for government policy. More than 8.6 trillion won has been drawn from the insurance fund for measures including emergency medical support and hospital restructuring. Such transfers may be defensible in an emergency, but repeated reliance on them blurs the line between social insurance and general taxation. More government funding alone will not make premium increases unnecessary. Korea’s per capita health spending, at $5,099 on a purchasing-power-parity basis, remains below the OECD average of $6,097. An aging society will require more resources. Higher premiums may therefore be unavoidable. But additional revenue should come with a more disciplined healthcare system. Korea needs stronger primary care and better management of chronic disease, while expensive tertiary hospitals should concentrate on serious and complex cases. Wasteful testing, duplicate treatment and improper claims also deserve closer scrutiny. A fee-for-service system makes cost control harder as an aging population requires more frequent treatment and more complex care. Alternative revenues, such as the Center for Market Education’s proposal to raise cigarette prices, could provide some breathing room. Useful as that may be, it is a buffer, not a long-term financing model. The government should first make its 20 percent obligation enforceable against settled revenue figures rather than flexible estimates. It should also require legislative approval for major transfers from National Health Insurance Service reserves to broader government programs. Korea’s health insurance problem is both demographic and institutional. Before asking citizens to pay higher premiums, the government should stop putting less into the system than the law requires. A sustainable safety net begins with an honest ledger, rather than price increases that merely paper over the underlying fiscal strain. Samsung Honam semiconductor and large conglomerate bonus demands clearly excluded from scope of collective action
Concerns and criticism raised over decision to narrow scope in executive decree
editorial.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung has repeatedly instructed that the scope of dispute subjects under the Yellow Envelope Act (amendments to Articles 2 and 3 of the Trade Union Act) be clarified through executive orders. editorials.title: [사설] 청년 취업자 45개월째 감소…정말 심각하다
summary: 청년 취업자가 45개월 연속으로 감소하고 있다.
노동시장 구조 악화로 청년층의 일자리 기회가 급속도로 사라지고 있다.
정부의 적극적인 대책이 시급한 상황이다.
editorials.stance: 청년 취업난의 심각성을 인식하고 근본적인 해결책 마련을 촉구한다.
editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Youth Employment Declining for 45 Consecutive Months...This Is Dire
summaryTr: Youth employment has declined for 45 consecutive months.

Active government measures are urgently needed.
